St. Noah the Righteous

St. Righteous Noah · Noah

Period
Biblical primeval narrative; no absolute calendar dates assigned
Region
The world of the Genesis flood narrative
Titles / vocation
Righteous · Forefather
Commemoration
Sunday of the Holy Forefathers (Sunday falling December 11–17 on the church calendar)

Introduction

St. Noah is remembered for the ark, the flood and God’s covenant, and is named among the righteous Forefathers in the Orthodox calendar.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundThe ark, flood and covenantDeathCommemoration and Christian interpretationChronology
Death / martyrdom

Death at 950 in Genesis 9:29; no martyrdom described

Read circumstances and sources

Background

Genesis introduces St. Noah as a righteous man in a world marked by violence and corruption. God commands him to build an ark for his household and living creatures. His response is described as obedience to the command he receives.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Genesis 6:5–22

The ark, flood and covenant

The narrative recounts entry into the ark, the flood, the receding waters and Noah’s sending of birds to learn whether the land is dry. After leaving the ark he offers sacrifice. God gives a covenant concerning the earth and places the rainbow as its sign. Genesis also records a later episode of drunkenness, so the narrative is not a claim that every action of his life was faultless.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Genesis 7–9

Death

Genesis gives St. Noah’s lifespan as 950 years and records his death. The narrative does not describe martyrdom, and this profile does not convert its chronology into an independently established modern date.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Genesis 9:28–29

Commemoration and Christian interpretation

The OCA commemorates St. Noah among the Forefathers and identifies the ark as a figure of the Church. A figure or type is an earlier event understood to anticipate a later saving reality.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Opening identification and interpretation of the ark

First Peter connects the flood and deliverance through water with baptism, while Hebrews presents Noah’s action as an example of faith.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · 1 Peter 3:20–21; Hebrews 11:7
